# list_issues MCP default page can be hours-stale for freshness sweeps

## Context

During the 2026-07-20 same-identity herd (two parallel Iris sessions), both sessions ran the `ticket-create` Content Sweep (i) honestly and still filed duplicates (#15596 / neomjs/neo#15597). The collision itself fit inside the irreducible create-gap (the `#12856` two-phase claim→recheck→execute anchor), and the tiebreak resolved it cleanly. But the post-incident V-B-A surfaced a second, independent safeguard degradation: the MCP `list_issues` call — explicitly sanctioned by `ticket-create-workflow.md` §1a(i) as an equivalent to `gh issue list` — returned a first page that did **not** surface issues filed hours earlier, on two independent calls.

## The Problem

Verified observations (2026-07-20, Iris seat):

1. **11:02Z sweep** (`list_issues`, limit 20, projection summary): first result neomjs/neo#15592 (updated 2026-07-19T21:37Z). neomjs/neo#15596 was filed 11:04:53Z — genuinely absent because it did not exist yet. Sweep honest; gap window.
2. **12:51Z check** (`list_issues`, limit 6, projection title_only): first page STILL starts at neomjs/neo#15592 (updated Jul 19 21:37Z) and contains nothing newer — while neomjs/neo#15599 (11:48Z), neomjs/neo#15598 (11:48Z), neomjs/neo#15596 (11:04Z) all exist and carry same-day update activity. A live `UPDATED_AT DESC` page cannot look like this; the served page is materially stale.
3. **gh CLI contrast** (`gh issue list --state open --limit 8 --json number,createdAt`, same minute): correctly returns neomjs/neo#15599, neomjs/neo#15598, neomjs/neo#15596 on top — created-descending, live.
4. **KB lineage**: the tool's default sort is documented as `UPDATED_AT DESC` via `IssueService.listIssues` → `GraphqlService.query(FETCH_ISSUES_LIST)`; a prior first-page defect (assignee filter searching only page one) was already called a "collision generator" and fixed server-side (`#15220` / `#14434` line). The staleness observed here is a distinct, unfixed behavior of the same surface — root cause (cache, memoized first page, or query construction) is part of the work.

Net: an agent using the sanctioned "equivalent MCP call" for the freshness sweep can receive a page missing hours of fresh filings — exactly the thundering-herd window the gate exists to catch. The `gh` path in the skill text is correct; the "equivalent MCP tool or GitHub API call" clause is not currently trustworthy for this gate.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.agents/skills/ticket-create/references/ticket-create-workflow.md` §1a(i) — the live freshness sweep mandate + the equivalence clause.
- `ai/mcp/server/github-workflow/` — `IssueService.listIssues` / `GraphqlService` `FETCH_ISSUES_LIST` (sort + paging + any response caching; the staleness root cause lives here).
- Prior fix lineage for the same tool surface: `#15220`, `#14434` (assignee-filter first-page defect, fixed server-side with truncation reporting).

## The Fix

Two independent deliverables, one ticket:

1. **Skill text (substrate, small):** amend §1a(i) so the equivalence clause requires *live, created-descending* evidence — the `gh issue list` command already satisfies it; the MCP `list_issues` call is only acceptable once deliverable 2 lands. Add one sentence naming the observed failure mode (stale first page across the herd window).
2. **Tool investigation + fix (github-workflow MCP):** root-cause why the default `list_issues` page served hours-old results twice (cache? memoization? query shape) and fix or document-with-warning. Server-side per the `#15220` / `#14434` precedent.

| `ticket-create-workflow.md` §1a(i) | skill payload (current text) | Equivalence clause requires live created-desc evidence; gh path named as the reference | MCP path allowed only after deliverable 2 | skill text itself | this incident |
| `list_issues` MCP tool | github-workflow server code + KB-documented `UPDATED_AT DESC` default | First page surfaces fresh filings (live ordering), or carries an explicit staleness/truncation signal | warning documented in tool description if unfixed | tool handbook | two observations above + gh contrast |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — sweep-discipline text + tool behavior fix; no ADR conflict.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] §1a(i) equivalence clause amended (live created-desc requirement + observed failure mode named)
- [ ] MCP `list_issues` staleness root-caused and fixed, or an explicit staleness/truncation signal added to the response
- [ ] Regression evidence: a fresh filing appears in the tool's first page within the herd window (test or documented live probe)
- [ ] (if tool code changes) unit coverage for the fixed path

## Out of Scope

- Redesigning the two-phase claim→recheck→execute discipline (the create-gap mitigation already exists and worked as designed via the tiebreak).
- `list_pull_requests` or other list tools' paging audits (separate tickets if the same root cause surfaces there).

## Avoided Traps

- **Treating the herd collision as proof the sweep text is broken** — the sweeps were honest; the collision fit the designed create-gap. This ticket is scoped to the *independent* staleness degradation only.
- **Silently swapping the skill to gh-only without fixing the tool** — hides a server-side defect other consumers may hit.

### @neo-kimi-iris - 2026-07-22T09:47:20Z

**Third live observation (2026-07-22, ~09:25Z, Iris seat) — same stale-page signature.** `list_issues` (limit 8, projection title): first page anchored at neomjs/neo#15681 with **#13796 at position 2** — an issue whose `updatedAt` is **2026-07-06T13:22:30Z** — while neomjs/neo#15678 (filed today, 2026-07-22 ~01:56Z, open) is absent from the page. A live `UPDATED_AT DESC` page cannot have a 16-day-untouched issue at position 2 ahead of same-day filings. This is the third observation after the two documented in the body, and the first since the root cause was identified.

**Root cause (identified today):** an issues connection carrying `filterBy: {assignee: null}` is routed by GitHub through a stale, hours-lagged read path; the identical connection omitting `filterBy` entirely returns the live page (`after: null` exonerated as the trigger). Fix shape: query selected by assignee *presence* — `FETCH_ISSUES_LIST` (filtered) vs `FETCH_ISSUES_LIST_NO_FILTER` — never passing a null-valued argument.

**Same-identity herd note:** a parallel Iris session holds the implementation (uncommitted worktree diff covering `IssueService.mjs`, `queries/issueQueries.mjs`, `openWorkCensusReader.mjs` + both specs, on branch `agent/15603-listissues-stale-page`). Per the neomjs/neo#15596/#15597 tiebreak precedent the implementation lane is yielded to that session; this session (the ticket author) ports evidence + review-support. Deliverable 1 (the §1a(i) skill-text amendment) flagged to the driver so the PR covers both deliverables.

- 2026-08-05T07:40:56Z @tobiu referenced in commit `30338b4` - "fix(ai): a marked SDK-boundary exception unfreezes the corpus, and a spec expires it (#16495) (#16496)

* fix(ai): a marked SDK-boundary exception unfreezes the corpus, and a spec expires it (#16488)

The Data Sync "GitHub Workflow corpus" stage cannot load `ai/services.mjs`: the
barrel eagerly imports 65 modules, two of which import `chromadb` at module scope,
and `chromadb` ships only in the Brain install tier. So a Body-tier CI job fails at
module resolution before any code runs. Twelve consecutive failures.

What that actually freezes is wider than the failing stage. `resources/content/issues`
and `resources/content/discussions` both last changed 2026-08-02T20:41:06Z — the same
commit, the moment the streak began. @neo-opus-vega measured the consequence: the
duplicate-sweep FALLBACK in `ticket-create-workflow.md` §1a reads that mirror, so it
silently describes a world without seven tickets filed since. §1a's own empirical
anchor is #15603, where a stale filtered-read path lagged the tracker by days. The
mandatory sweep is a live `gh` read, so the gate itself is not open — the compromised
surfaces are the fallback and semantic retrieval.

The correct fix is deferring those two leaf imports, which is an initialization
refactor of both Chroma managers with ~20 external readers of `.client` plus a
documented test seam. That is deliberately not bundled into a pipeline restore.

So this is a narrow, deliberate exception at the one failing site, carrying BOTH
guarantees the barrel supplied: the Neo namespace bootstrap, and the forced
`syncOnStartup = false` override — which is NOT redundant with the config leaf's own
`false` default, because the override holds regardless of env or overlay and
`SyncService` branches on it. Dropping it would let an overlay turn a read-only
emission run into a bi-directional sync.

**The exception expires mechanically, not by comment.** A retirement trigger keyed to
an event nothing observes can never fire while reading as coverage — the condition
@neo-opus-vega set, and the same silent drift that produced this defect.
`syncGithubWorkflowImportException.spec.mjs` walks static imports from the barrel and
FAILS the moment it stops reaching `chromadb`, naming exactly what to delete. Proven
rather than asserted: deferring the three `chromadb` imports turns it red with
"ai/services.mjs NO LONGER reaches chromadb ... This failure is the exception expiring
on schedule, not a regression."

Two further guards, both phrased so failure means "delete or revisit", never "add more
exception": the site must keep both barrel-supplied guarantees, and the two methods
this script calls must stay absent from the github-workflow OpenAPI spec — if either
is added, `makeSafe` would start validating it and the direct import silently drops
that.

Measured: the stage entry now walks 56 modules and reaches no `chromadb`, against 259
reaching it via `services.mjs -> DatabaseService -> ChromaManager`.

Co-Authored-By: Vega <neo-opus-vega@neomjs.com>

* test(ai): assert the stage entry does NOT reach chromadb — the property that actually broke (#16495)

Addresses @neo-gpt's Request Changes on PR #16496.

The spec guarded the exception's EXPIRY and its carried invariants, and never the
production property. `reachesPackage` was called only with BARREL; `EXCEPTION_SITE`
was declared and never walked.

So the guard proved the exception is still NEEDED and said nothing about whether it
still WORKS. A future static import from any module this stage already depends on
back to `chromadb` would turn the hourly stage red again while every assertion in the
file stayed green — a guard covering the retirement path but not the failure it was
built for. That is the gap, and the review named it exactly.

The new witness walks EXCEPTION_SITE and requires `reached === false`, with the same
positive control the barrel test uses: assert `walked > 50` FIRST, because an empty
walk makes `reached === false` vacuously true and a moved or unreadable entry file
would read as "clean" — the shape this whole file exists to reject.

RED proven against the real regression rather than a synthetic one: restoring dev's
`import {GH_Config, GH_SyncService} from '../../services.mjs'` fails it with the
production chain printed verbatim —

  syncGithubWorkflow.mjs -> ai/services.mjs
    -> ai/services/knowledge-base/DatabaseService.mjs
    -> ai/services/knowledge-base/ChromaManager.mjs -> chromadb

which is the identical path in the CI failure ("imported from
ai/services/knowledge-base/ChromaManager.mjs"). The invariants test fails alongside
it, since the barrel import also drops the bootstrap and the syncOnStartup override.

The failure message says "break the new edge — do NOT widen the exception", keeping
this file's rule that every failure here means delete-or-repair, never add-more-exception.

Co-Authored-By: Euclid <neo-gpt@neomjs.com>
